quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #18
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: You should allow extra space in front of your vehicle when following a:

options.text: Station wagon.
Passenger vehicle.
Motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles can stop faster than other vehicles. You need extra space to stop safely if the motorcycle brakes suddenly. Also, motorcycles are hard to see at night because they have only one tail light.

questions.question: You are parking downhill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Straight ahead
Right, toward the side of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the side of the road
questions.explanation: When parking downhill on any road, or uphill on a road with no curb, turn your wheels toward the edge of the road. This way, your car will roll away from traffic if the brakes fail. When parking uphill on a road with a curb, turn your wheels toward the center so the car rolls into the curb.

questions.question: You see pedestrians near the road. What should you do?

options.text: Sound your horn and keep your speed.
Speed up to get past them quickly.
Slow down and pass carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and pass carefully.
questions.explanation: Watch for pedestrians who may walk into your path. When you see pedestrians near the road, slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.question: When entering an interstate highway, you should:

options.text: Stop, check for cars, and enter when safe.
Check for cars and reduce your speed to 25 mph before entering the traffic lane.
Check for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Do not stop when entering a highway like you would on other roads. Use the acceleration lane to speed up and match the traffic. Then merge smoothly when it is safe.

questions.question: To turn quickly, where should your hands be on the steering wheel?

options.text: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
Next to each other on top of the steering wheel.
On the top and bottom of the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: Place both hands on opposite sides of the steering wheel. This position is comfortable and lets you turn safely at high speeds.

questions.question: When driving behind another vehicle at night, what should you do with your headlights?

options.text: Use low beams.
Use high beams until you are within 10 feet of the vehicle.
Use high beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use low beams.
questions.explanation: Use high beams only in rural areas when no other cars are nearby. Switch to low beams when following another vehicle closely.

questions.question: What are the rules for bicycles on the road?

options.text: Bicycles must always yield to motor vehicles.
Bicycles do not have to follow traffic rules.
Bicycles are vehicles with the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bicycles are vehicles with the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicles.
questions.explanation: Bicycles are considered vehicles on the road. They have the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicles. Drivers should respect bicyclists' rights.

questions.question: You hit a parked vehicle and cannot find the owner. What must you do?

options.text: Call your insurance company when you get home.
Wait for the owner to return.
Leave a note with your name and address on the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a note with your name and address on the vehicle.
questions.explanation: If you hit a parked vehicle or other property, you must leave a note with your name, phone number, and address on the vehicle or property you hit.

questions.question: Drowsiness affects driving the same way as alcohol and drugs. It can:

options.text: Help you be a better driver.
Make you feel better.
Impair your judgment.

questions.correctAnswerText: Impair your judgment.
questions.explanation: Not getting enough sleep causes poor driving. Like drugs and alcohol, drowsiness slows your reaction time, reduces awareness, and impairs judgment.

questions.question: When should you use your horn?

options.text: When another vehicle is in your way.
When it may help prevent a collision.
When another driver makes a mistake.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it may help prevent a collision.
questions.explanation: Use your horn only to prevent collisions. Do not use your horn to tell other drivers to go faster or to get out of your way.

questions.question: A train has passed and you are stopped at a railroad crossing. What should you do?

options.text: Wait until the signal lights stop flashing.
Check for a second train.
Do both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do both of the above.
questions.explanation: After a train passes, watch for another train on any track. Do not drive until all gates are raised and all warning lights have stopped flashing.

questions.question: What does this white sign mean?

options.text: The railroad crossing is controlled. Keep your normal speed.
Look and listen. Be ready to stop if needed.
Stop at the railroad tracks and wait for a signal before crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look and listen. Be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: When you see a railroad crossing ahead, look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop. Let any trains pass before you go.

questions.question: When driving on snow or ice, what should you do?

options.text: It is safe to use cruise control.
Change speed and direction slowly and carefully.
Drive the same way you do in normal conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change speed and direction slowly and carefully.
questions.explanation: On snow or ice, make all speed and direction changes slowly. Never use cruise control on snow or ice because your tires may lose grip on the road and you could lose control of your vehicle.

questions.question: Two drivers reach a four-way stop sign at the same time. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on the right.
The driver on the left.
One driver may go without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right.
questions.explanation: If two drivers arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, let the driver on your right go first. You can go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Road construction or maintenance area ahead.
Side road.
Railroad ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road construction or maintenance area ahead.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn of hazards. Orange signs are used in construction and maintenance areas.

questions.question: You are entering an interstate highway. What should you do?

options.text: Find a safe opening and merge into traffic.
Merge across two lanes at once.
Always stop before entering the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe opening and merge into traffic.
questions.explanation: When merging, find a gap large enough to safely enter the flow of traffic. Do not stop on the entrance ramp unless there is no safe gap to merge into.

questions.question: If you drive slower than other traffic, what will most likely happen?

options.text: You will block traffic and may get a ticket.
You will improve traffic flow.
You will show good defensive driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will block traffic and may get a ticket.
questions.explanation: Slow down in heavy traffic or bad weather. But if you drive so slowly that you block traffic, you may get a ticket. Drive at the speed of traffic unless traffic is above the speed limit.

questions.question: You are following a large truck on the freeway. How should you drive?

options.text: Stay close in bad weather because the truck driver can see farther ahead.
Stay farther back than you would behind a regular car.
Stay one car length behind so the driver can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther back than you would behind a regular car.
questions.explanation: If you follow a truck too closely, the driver cannot see you in the mirrors. Tailgating is dangerous because you lose your safety space if the truck stops quickly.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Trucks entering.
Truck exit only.
A steep downhill slope is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A steep downhill slope is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep downhill slope is coming. Check your brakes before going down.

questions.question: A solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line means passing is:

options.text: Allowed from the side with the solid yellow line.
Not allowed from either direction.
Allowed from the side with the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allowed from the side with the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: When a solid yellow line is next to a broken yellow line, you can pass from the side with the broken line. You cannot pass from the side with the solid line.

questions.question: Which statement about large trucks is true?

options.text: They take longer to stop than passenger vehicles.
They all have air brakes that let them stop quickly.
They are easier to turn than passenger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They take longer to stop than passenger vehicles.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need more time to stop than other vehicles at the same speed. A passenger vehicle going 55 mph can stop in about 400 feet. A large truck at 55 mph needs almost 800 feet to stop.

questions.question: When is a U-turn not allowed?

options.text: In a parking lot.
On or near any curve or hill.
On a straight road where you can see clearly for 500 feet in both directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: On or near any curve or hill.
questions.explanation: Never turn around on or near curves or hills. You cannot see oncoming traffic or pedestrians, which could cause a crash.

questions.question: Where is it safe to pass another vehicle?

options.text: In an intersection if there are no oncoming vehicles.
Only where signs and markings allow passing.
In a curve if there are no oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only where signs and markings allow passing.
questions.explanation: Never pass in intersections, parking lots, or alleys. Do not pass on curves or hills where you cannot see oncoming traffic. Pass only where signs and markings permit it, and only if you have enough safe space.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing, you must:

options.text: Watch for vehicles that must stop (school buses, trucks with hazardous materials, etc.).
Watch for trains from multiple directions.
Do both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do both of the above.
questions.explanation: Approach all railroad crossings with caution. Cross only when you are sure no train is coming from either direction. Watch for vehicles that must stop at crossings, like school buses and trucks carrying hazardous materials.

questions.question: What do rumble strips do?

options.text: They warn drivers about tire problems.
They test a vehicle's shock absorbers.
They create vibration and noise to alert drivers that they are leaving the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They create vibration and noise to alert drivers that they are leaving the road.
questions.explanation: Rumble strips make noise and vibration to warn sleepy or distracted drivers that they are leaving the road or approaching a stop sign or signal.

questions.question: How can you avoid becoming an aggressive driver?

options.text: Stay calm and focus on driving.
Drive faster than the posted speed limit.
Follow closely behind the car in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and focus on driving.
questions.explanation: To avoid aggressive driving, stay calm and focus on the road. Do not take other drivers' actions personally. Plan enough time for your trip, obey speed limits, and be patient with other drivers.

questions.question: Switch to low beam headlights when you are within ____ of another driver.

options.text: 1,000 feet
500 feet
200 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 500 feet
questions.explanation: You must use low beams when you are within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle or following another vehicle. High beams blind other drivers and make the road unsafe.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on the highway, you should:

options.text: Stop in the right lane.
Park with all four wheels off the road if possible.
Stop where you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park with all four wheels off the road if possible.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle breaks down, park with all four wheels off the main road if you can.

questions.question: What does a double solid yellow line down the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is allowed.
Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is not allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is not allowed.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Solid lines mean you cannot pass.

questions.question: At a red light with a green arrow, when can you go?

options.text: After you come to a complete stop.
When the light changes.
If you are in the correct lane and the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you are in the correct lane and the road is clear.
questions.explanation: If you are in a lane with a green arrow, you can go in that direction when the road is clear. This is true whether the arrow appears alone or with other signals.
